title: One full round trip of a function call: ask, validate, execute, reply

events.label: Ask a question
events.detail: "What was last quarter's total order value for East China?" — the model cannot answer this itself: the order data lives in the business database. All the model can do is request a query.

events.label: Declare the tool list
events.detail: The request's tools array declares get_order_total: name (the function name), description (an explanation written for the model), and input_schema (parameter constraints as JSON Schema). The declaration travels with the request; the model never touches any real code.

events.label: Send the request (tools + question)
events.detail: The only difference from an ordinary chat request is one extra tools field — tools are not plugins installed into the model, they are a list of functions shipped with every request.

events.label: The model returns a tool_use request
events.detail: The output is not prose but a structured tool_use block: {"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01A","name":"get_order_total","input":{"region":"East China","quarter":"Q2"}}. type marks the block kind, id is this request's unique handle, name points into the declared list, and input holds parameters the model generated from the schema; stop_reason=tool_use means "I am waiting for the result".

events.label: Validate the parameters
events.detail: The client validates input against input_schema: region and quarter are well-typed and among the allowed values. Validation comes before execution — the parameters a model generates are never taken at face value.

events.label: Execute the query
events.detail: The execution code is written by the application: assemble the SQL, connect to the database, run it. This step happens outside the model's world — the model never touches the network itself.

events.label: Query result returns
events.detail: The database returns the aggregate: East China's Q2 order total is ¥4,182,000. The tool function formats it as text.

events.label: Reply with a tool_result
events.detail: A tool_result block is appended to messages: {"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"toolu_01A","content":"¥4,182,000"}. tool_use_id must pair with the request — it is the only clue telling the model which result answers which request.

events.label: Final answer
events.detail: With the result in context, the model writes the answer in natural language and stop_reason=end_turn — no new requests, so this round can wrap up.

events.label: Deliver the answer with its provenance
events.detail: The answer carries its provenance (the query that ran and when). The user sees one sentence; behind it sits a complete ask-validate-execute-reply round trip.

events.label: Write the audit log
events.detail: tool_use and tool_result pairs go into the log: who requested what and when, what the client executed, what came back. Auditability is the design dividend of keeping execution authority on the client.
